mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over the next month reduces the discount rate applied to expected future dividends, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite the FEDFUNDS increase, with a t-statistic exceeding 1.5.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs signals labor market strengthening, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 200,000 in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or flat, and 10-day moving average of consumer confidence (UMich) shows no improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 2% in a month indicates weakening demand for manufactured goods, which compresses earnings growth forecasts and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 2% in a single month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns exceed +2% despite the INDPRO decline, with a t-statistic below -1.0.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising consumer price indexes (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signal accelerating inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain higher policy rates, which reduces equity discount rates and yields negative 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains above 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05), or CPIAUCSL reverts below 3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%, the expected future path of policy rates is perceived as flatter, lowering real discount rates and generating positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.10), or the 3-month FEDFUNDS trend reverses downward.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) below 150,000 suggests labor market softening, lowering consumer sentiment and corporate earnings growth forecasts, which results in negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below 150,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or flat, and 7-day moving average of consumer sentiment (UMich) shows improvement.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence (UMich) create a dual-demand shock that amplifies earnings downgrades and investor uncertainty, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns when both signals are present.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite both INDPRO decline and UNRATE decline being statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a post-shock recovery regime (defined by UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS < 5%), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days are more likely to be positive as policy remains accommodative and labor market shows slow healing.
failure_condition: The regime condition holds but 20-day forward returns are negative, or the regime is not confirmed by at least two consecutive months of UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS < 5%.
